core.text: Host: the existing Endless Museum. Keep museum encounters, tutorial learning and critical-poetic writing as overlapping sets. Teach selected reusable operations; name supplied support. Keep decisions, proposals, evidence and unknowns distinct. Preserve why a choice was made. Move project → sequence → hall → source → sequence → project. Keep summary work separate from explicitly authorized museum implementation. A summary alone does not authorize code, hall-order or full-lesson edits. The memory interface is a tool for this work.
core.reason: Repeated local rewrites lost the museum setting and prior author decisions. Compact instructions should preserve intent and support changes without flattening artistic differences.
core.open_question: Which sequence boundary should receive the next deliberate reading? Preserve mature sequences unless evidence gives a reason to reopen them.

sequence:primitives.summary: Arrival → represented point → coordinates → relation → retained list → grid address → face → connected faces → generated form → limit → composition.
sequence:primitives.reason: A usable material travels onward. The closing halls can reflect and compose rather than introduce more syntax.
sequence:primitives.open_question: Where should each reduced learner construction run inside the existing museum?

map:Point_Line_Grid.summary: Fit the accepted drawing, then round display positions. Keep source data separate.
map:Point_Line_Grid.reason: This is the concrete return from a recorded list to lattice addresses; it also constrains the later Array analogy.
map:Point_Line_Grid.open_question: How should the lesson make source position and displayed address visible without overloading the learner?

findings.text: Keep the lineage open to change. Show the current order and complete summaries together, while preserving alternatives, reasons and open questions. A hall may contribute through reflection or an encounter without introducing a new programming step.
findings.reason: Palle approved the continuous outline on 4 October 2026 with the instruction: “keep the freedom of change.” The interface should support reconsideration as the project evolves.
findings.sequence_effect: Compare neighbouring halls and question their order or teaching selection without silently rewriting the authored route.
findings.project_effect: Keep museum, tutorial and critical writing as overlapping sets. A memory structure is an aid to judgment, not a fixed curriculum.
findings.method: Explicit author instruction in this conversation, 4 October 2026; a design decision, not a source or runtime observation.
findings.review_note: Retained as an explicit author instruction for the memory interface. This records the requested freedom to reconsider choices; it makes no runtime or whole-curriculum claim.

findings.text: Separate the closing Primitives encounters: generated forms / tighter Ignorance -> Godot's supplied mesh forms -> exploration with columns and letter profiles -> Portals (finite approximations and chosen tolerance) -> Melencolia. Retain Coordinates, Trace and Grid in the opening lineage. Give exploration distinct space: first compare one profile at 4, 6, 8, 12 and 16 radial segments, then vary outline and height; use letter profiles to expose inherited outlines, holes and new bodily uses. This is a route proposal, not a changed sequence.
findings.reason: Palle identifies Ignorance as too dense and asks for a clearer exploratory direction. Its current manuscript and map combine the Platonic courtyard, sphere comparisons, cost display, capsule and engine mesh library. The existing Primitives_Godot map is outside the authored sequence. Columns and glyph studies provide concrete material for a separate exploration encounter.
findings.sequence_effect: Let construction, borrowed engine forms, artistic choices, limits and meaning have distinct moments. The column lesson can reuse lists, loops and a supplied sampler; the glyph geometry builder can remain supplied. Do not imply that arbitrary profile sweeps are built-in PrimitiveMesh types. Pi is finite; an endless decimal expansion, polygon convergence and a philosophical ideal are distinct. Do not turn Melencolia into another syntax lesson.
findings.project_effect: Use sequence review to redistribute attention while preserving the wider artifact ecology. Keep the source-supported inventory separate from the curatorial judgment and a future VR assessment. Do not force every object into a tutorial or remove older works just to match a reduced summary.
findings.method: Author proposal plus parallel read-only review of authored route, selected texts and placement data; visual inspection of earlier native Godot captures. Column gallery is marked standalone/not map-ready; glyph gallery is isolated with a non-colliding camera. No new runtime or headset test. Museum hosting, passages and comfort remain to be checked before VR delivery.
findings.review_note: Palle explicitly approved expanding the sequence with these maps on 4 October 2026. This accepts the direction; the original source hashes remain as the proposal evidence. Implementation and checks are recorded separately.

findings.text: Installed Primitives_Godot, Primitives_Columns and Primitives_Profiles between Ignorance and Portals. Library and seven-form choir move from Ignorance; its other 26 placements remain. Columns: five controlled specimens then twenty varied bodies. Profiles: six original glyph forms with source outlines. Preserve the existing museum-only biome stop after Portals. Fifteen book halls; sixteen museum stops. Full tutorial development remains separate.
findings.reason: Author approved the proposed split so engine vocabulary and exploration have their own spatial attention instead of further densifying Ignorance.
findings.sequence_effect: Generated form -> supplied engine forms -> column choices -> borrowed outlines -> finite refinement -> composition. Earlier Coordinates, Trace and Grid retain their places.
findings.project_effect: Source-backed plan, actual museum placement and current summaries agree for the added halls. The wider collection is retained. Native checks do not establish headset comfort or learning.
findings.method: 26 source-chain/preservation checks; native Godot room loads, central player walks and floor rays in all three new halls; 63 checks across four production portal transitions using explicit crossing requests. Original artifact mesher/recipes retained. No headset or learner trial.
findings.review_note: Recorded the authorized implementation and its bounded native evidence. Remaining VR comfort and learner edit-host questions stay open.
